story: The University of Alaska's AI rulebook. A mandatory Generative AI Security Standard has bound every user of UA computing resources since January 2025, while the system's own policies page still says regulations are under development and a Board of Regents policy is expected in November.

claims.claim: The UA Generative AI Security Standard carries an effective date of January 2025.
claims.verbatim: Effective: January 2025
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Date line block on the standard itself. The page also carries a separate line reading Approved January 2025, recorded as C02.

claims.claim: The standard was approved in January 2025.
claims.verbatim: Approved: January 2025
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Approval and effect share the same month, so the deck should not present them as two milestones.

claims.claim: The standard was updated in March 2025 to include material from content area experts.
claims.verbatim: Updated: March 2025 (included material from content-area experts)
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: The parenthetical is part of the printed line and should be kept if the line is quoted.

claims.claim: The standard sets its next review for January 2027.
claims.verbatim: Next Review: January 2027
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Strong deck material. The binding rule is not scheduled for review until after the regents policy is due to be voted.

claims.claim: Information Security and Assurance Standards are mandatory and apply to the UA System and all users of UA computing resources.
claims.value: all users of UA computing resources
claims.verbatim: Information Security and Assurance (ISA) Standards are mandatory and apply to the UA System and all users of UA computing resources.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: This is the scope sentence. It describes the ISA standard class generally, which this document belongs to, rather than naming generative AI in the same sentence.

claims.claim: The standard states that it supplements and supports Board of Regents Policy and Regulation R02.07.
claims.verbatim: This standard supplements and supports Board of Regents Policy & Regulation R02.07.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Answers whether the standard hangs off a numbered regents policy. It does.

claims.claim: The standard cites Board of Regents Policy and Regulation R02.07.060 as the requirement to secure University Information Resources.
claims.verbatim: In an effort to perform its requirements under Board of Regents Policy & Regulation R02.07.060 to secure University Information Resources
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Quoted as a fragment because the printed sentence continues. Use as partial quotation or paraphrase.

claims.claim: Board of Regents chapter 02.07 is titled Information Resources.
claims.verbatim: Chapter 02.07. Information Resources
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Board of Regents
claims.notes: Corroborates C06 and C07 from the regents own policy index. No artificial intelligence policy appears in this chapter listing.

claims.claim: Systems that fail to abide by approved information security controls may face disconnection from the UA network.
claims.verbatim: systems and services which fail to abide by approved information security controls may be subject to the implementation of compensating controls to effectively manage risk, up to and including disconnection from the UA network
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: The operative word is may, not will. The sentence targets systems and services rather than individual people. Keep the conditional if quoted.

claims.claim: Violations may subject employees to disciplinary action up to and including termination.
claims.verbatim: may subject employees to disciplinary action, up to and including termination
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Confirmed across two independent extractions. Conditional may must be preserved.

claims.claim: Violations may subject students to disciplinary action including expulsion.
claims.verbatim: may subject students to disciplinary action including expulsion
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: One extraction rendered a longer tail referencing the Student Code of Conduct. The shorter string is the one confirmed twice.

claims.claim: The standard defines Public data by reference to Board of Regents Regulation R02.07.093 as data that can be freely shared with the public.
claims.verbatim: Data classified as Public as defined by Board of Regents Regulation R02.07.093 can be freely shared with the public and posted on publicly viewable web pages.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: The classification scheme lives in regents regulation R02.07.093, a different number from R02.07.060 in C07.

claims.claim: The standard describes Internal Use data as generally not available to parties outside the University of Alaska community.
claims.verbatim: Data classified as Internal Use as defined by Board of Regents Regulation R02.07.093 is generally not available to parties outside the University of Alaska community
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Partial quotation. Do not append a prohibition clause to it, see C16.

claims.claim: The standard describes Restricted data as subject to disclosure laws and warranting careful management and protection.
claims.verbatim: Data classified as Restricted as defined by Board of Regents R02.07.093 may be subject to disclosure laws and warrants careful management and protection
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: Partial quotation. This instance omits the word Regulation before R02.07.093, which is how the page prints it.

claims.claim: The standard warns that sensitive information provided to generative AI can be stored on servers the University of Alaska does not control.
claims.value: servers not controlled by the University of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: The fact-checker's extraction carried an ellipsis not present in the source, so no verbatim is recorded here. PARAPHRASE ONLY on a slide.

claims.claim: The standard does not flatly forbid Internal or Restricted data from generative AI and instead requires such use to meet published requirements for data storage, computing environments and model deployment.
claims.verbatim: must meet published requirements for data storage, computing environments, and model deployment
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Office of Information Technology
claims.notes: CORRECTION of the brief. A first pass read the page as prohibiting Internal and Restricted data outright. A targeted re-read found no such sentence. The regime is conditional. The deck must never say banned or forbidden.

claims.claim: The University GenAI Policies and Guidelines page carries a last updated stamp of 03/11/2025.
claims.verbatim: Last Updated: 03/11/2025
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska
claims.notes: The policies page has not been restamped in roughly eighteen months while the regents debate a policy.

claims.claim: The University GenAI Policies and Guidelines page states that UA System regulations are currently under development.
claims.verbatim: UA System regulations are currently under development.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska
claims.notes: Confirmed verbatim on two separate extractions. The spine of the story, sitting beside a mandatory standard in force since January 2025.

claims.claim: The University GenAI Policies and Guidelines page says adoption and use of these tools are guided by individual university and department policies that are currently under development.
claims.verbatim: The adoption and use of these tools are guided by individual university and department policies, currently under development.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska
claims.notes: Softer than the others. A second extraction showed a near identical classroom variant, suggesting two similar sentences. Attribute to the page generally.

claims.claim: The main UA GenAI hub page carries a last updated stamp of 01/09/2026.
claims.verbatim: Last Updated: 01/09/2026
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska
claims.notes: Useful contrast with C17. The hub was refreshed in January while the policies subpage still reads March 2025.

claims.claim: KTOO reported on September 16th that the University of Alaska Board of Regents reviewed a draft artificial intelligence policy.
claims.verbatim: The University of Alaska's Board of Regents reviewed a draft artificial intelligence policy designed to require all three campuses to develop AI implementation plans for their communities.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Reported by Jamie Diep. The regents own agenda packet was not fetched, so this is single sourced reporting about a document nobody here read. Attribute to KTOO.

claims.claim: According to KTOO the draft policy would require all three University of Alaska campuses to develop an AI plan covering students, faculty and staff.
claims.verbatim: designed to require all three campuses to develop AI implementation plans for their communities
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: What the reporter says the draft requires, not language read in the draft. Phrase as according to KTOO.

claims.claim: KTOO reported that the draft policy's guiding principles are preserving human talent, safeguarding data security and using AI to expand educational access.
claims.verbatim: The policy's core principles focus on preserving human talent, safeguarding data security, and using AI to expand educational access.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Wording varied slightly between two extractions. Treat the three principles as reliable and the exact sentence as loose. Prefer paraphrase.

claims.claim: A 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey found that about 85 percent of college students use generative AI in their coursework.
claims.verbatim: It finds that about 85% of college students use generative AI in their coursework.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Secondary. KTOO attributes this to a 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey, which was not reached directly. NATIONAL figure about college students generally, NOT Alaska specific. A slide must never imply it measures UA students, and must keep the word about.

claims.claim: Ben Shier is the University of Alaska's Chief Information Technology Officer.
claims.verbatim: Ben Shier, the university's Chief Information Technology Officer
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Title confirmed identically on two extractions. Chief Information Technology Officer, not Chief Information Officer.

claims.claim: Shier told the regents that AI amplifies existing questions rather than raising new ones.
claims.verbatim: AI only amplifies some of those questions, but they're not necessarily new topics.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Direct quotation confirmed inside quotation marks on two extractions. Only this first sentence appeared in both, so this is the safe slide quote.

claims.claim: Shier said the university assesses tools against a data type and tells users where that data can and cannot be placed.
claims.verbatim: we assess the tools against health data and say these are the places where you can put that data into these tools and where you can't
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Direct quotation confirmed inside quotation marks on two extractions. Corroborates C16, the conditional rather than prohibitive posture.

claims.claim: KTOO reported that Shier said the university currently can't control and track every usage of AI.
claims.value: can't control and track every usage of AI
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: LOAD BEARING CORRECTION. This is the reporter's indirect speech and is NOT inside quotation marks. The deck may write that Shier said it, attributed to KTOO, but must NEVER put quotation marks around these words.

claims.claim: Regent Christine Ressler raised concerns about the university's ability to monitor AI use across the system.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Ressler is described but, on two extractions, is NOT quoted anywhere in the article. No words may be attributed to her as a quote. Reported paraphrase only, or omit.

claims.claim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft AI policy for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.verbatim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: A plan, not a scheduled vote. No day of the month is given and no primary agenda confirms it. Write is expected to or plans to, never will be voted on.

claims.claim: The university plans to collect student and community input through listening sessions and surveys this fall, with no session dates scheduled as of KTOO's report.
claims.verbatim: No session dates had been scheduled as of the article's publication.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Time sensitive and true only as of September 16th. Date stamp it on any slide.

claims.claim: The Board of Regents meeting where the draft AI policy was presented was held at the University of Alaska Southeast.
claims.verbatim: At the Board of Regents meeting at UAS, he said many questions sparked by AI are not new to the university.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO
claims.notes: Location confirmed as UAS. No exact meeting date is printed. Do not print a specific meeting date.

claims.claim: UAA Chancellor Cheryl Siemers wrote that UAA is launching AI@UAA this fall.
claims.verbatim: To advance this work, we are launching AI@UAA this fall.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: Primary, the chancellor writing on UAA's own site. Exact initiative name is AI@UAA with no spaces.

claims.claim: AI@UAA will be part of a new Leveraging Innovative Frameworks and Technologies Center, abbreviated LIFT.
claims.value: Leveraging Innovative Frameworks and Technologies (LIFT) Center
claims.verbatim: This initiative will be part of a new Leveraging Innovative Frameworks and Technologies (LIFT) Center, which will ensure coordinated and thoughtful AI implementation across all our campuses.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: Full expansion confirmed verbatim on two extractions. Across all our campuses here means UAA's campuses, not the whole UA system.

claims.claim: The UAA post announcing AI@UAA and the LIFT Center was written by Chancellor Cheryl Siemers and published on September 10th.
claims.verbatim: Cheryl Siemers, UAA Chancellor
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: Author and date confirmed on two extractions, and the date matches the URL path.

claims.claim: UAF policy states that work created by an artificial intelligence engine is covered by the student code of conduct.
claims.verbatim: Work that is created by an artificial intelligence engine is covered by the student code of conduct.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Office of Rights, Compliance and Accountability
claims.notes: Primary campus rule. Shows the rules exist campus by campus rather than systemwide.

claims.claim: UAF states that findings of responsibility will not be based solely on AI detection software at this time.
claims.verbatim: findings of responsibility will not be solely based on AI detection software at this time
claims.source_outlet: UAF Office of Rights, Compliance and Accountability
claims.notes: The phrase at this time is part of the quotation and signals a provisional stance. Keep it.

claims.claim: UAS guidance tells instructors to avoid relying on AI detection tools alone because the tools have high error rates.
claims.verbatim: Avoid relying on AI detection tools alone. These tools have high error rates and on their own are not sufficient as evidence.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Southeast Center for Excellence in Learning and Teaching
claims.notes: Corroborates C39 from a second campus. Most recently modified campus guidance found, stamped July 24th, 2026.

claims.claim: UAS guidance tells instructors that the key is to clearly communicate their AI policies to students.
claims.verbatim: No matter your stance on AI tools, the key is to clearly communicate your policies to your students.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Southeast Center for Excellence in Learning and Teaching
claims.notes: Shows the burden sits on the individual instructor, the practical consequence of C18 and C19.

claims.claim: UAF guidance tells faculty to clarify expectations for generative AI use up front in the syllabus.
claims.verbatim: Clarify your expectations for the use of generative AI up front in your syllabus.
claims.source_outlet: UAF Center for Teaching and Learning
claims.notes: Third campus corroborating the instructor by instructor pattern. No last modified date recovered, so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: UAA's IT page directs users to the university's policies on data classification, information security and privacy when using AI.
claims.verbatim: Users should reference the university's policies and guidance regarding data classification and compliance, information security, privacy, copyright implications and the potential for bias when using AI.
claims.source_outlet: UAA Information Technology Services
claims.notes: Confirms the standard in C01 is operationally referenced at campus level, not a dormant document.
